lead: Combustion is fast, hot and hidden inside metal. To see it, researchers build an engine with quartz or sapphire windows, light the inside with a laser, and film the light with a high-speed camera. Only a few syllabi teach this, because the hardware is costly. It is how spray shapes, flame speeds, soot clouds and the low-temperature strategies of HCCI and RCCI were understood.
prereq: You need: flame propagation (Combustion in SI and CI engines) and the soot steps of smoke and particulate matter.

sections.h3: An engine you can look into

blocks.text: Windows can sit in the head, the liner or the piston crown. Sapphire is stronger and passes more infrared; quartz is cheaper and passes ultraviolet, which laser methods need. In the Bowditch design the piston is extended and carries a window in its crown and a 45° mirror below it. Light from the chamber travels down the cylinder axis through the crown, and the mirror turns it sideways to a camera beside the engine, so the camera sees the whole bore from below.

An optical engine is not a production engine: its compression ratio is often lower, its walls are colder or hotter, the chamber is simplified and it is fired for short runs because soot and oil foul the windows. Those differences, not the short runs, change its cycle-to-cycle variation, so its images show mechanisms, not production numbers.

sections.h3: Light tuned to what you want to see

items: High-speed imaging of the flame’s own light shows flame growth and glowing soot.
Schlieren and shadowgraph turn density gradients into brightness, showing the flame front and the vapour edge of a spray.
Mie scattering from droplets is strong and shows the liquid spray; Rayleigh scattering from gas molecules is weak and gives density or temperature after calibration.
Laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) excites one chosen molecule (fuel tracer, OH, NO, formaldehyde) and maps where it is.
Laser-induced incandescence and two-colour pyrometry give soot amount and soot temperature.

Particle image velocimetry (PIV) correlates two images of seed particles to map the flow field in a plane; laser Doppler anemometry gives the velocity at one point, so swirl or tumble needs the point moved across the cylinder.

blocks.text: A laser sheet, not a beam, lights a plane: cylindrical lenses spread the beam into a sheet under a millimetre thick. Common sources are the Nd:YAG laser, whose 1064 nm output is frequency-doubled to 532 nm (green) or quadrupled to 266 nm, and excimer lasers in the ultraviolet, such as XeCl at 308 nm. The flame expansion speed from two frames is S = Δr ÷ Δt, where Δr is the growth of the flame radius and Δt the time between frames. It includes the push of the expanding burned gas, so it is larger than the burning velocity of the mixture.

examples.question: Two high-speed frames are 0.1 ms apart. The flame radius grows from 8 mm to 12 mm. The engine runs at 1500 rev/min. Find the flame expansion speed and the crank angle between the frames.
examples.answer: The flame front expands at 40 m/s, and the frames are 0.9° of crank angle apart.

traps: Quoting an optical-engine flame speed as a production value: the compression ratio, walls and chamber differ.
Treating a line-of-sight image as a slice: direct imaging and extinction add up light along the whole path.
Swapping Mie and Rayleigh: Mie comes from droplets and is strong; Rayleigh from gas molecules and is weak.
Giving 532 nm as the natural output of Nd:YAG: it is the doubled frequency of 1064 nm.

quiz.q: What does the Bowditch extended piston provide?
quiz.a: A window in the piston crown and a 45° mirror below it, so a camera beside the engine sees the chamber from below along the cylinder axis.

quiz.q: Why use a laser sheet rather than a beam?
quiz.a: A sheet lights one plane, so the camera records a two-dimensional slice; a beam lights only a line.

quiz.q: A flame radius grows from 10 mm to 14 mm in 0.2 ms. Find the flame expansion speed.
At 2000 rev/min, how many crank degrees pass in 0.1 ms?
A Mie image of a spray is bright, but a Rayleigh image of the same plane is weak. Why?
quiz.a: Mie light comes from droplets, which scatter strongly; Rayleigh light comes from gas molecules, which scatter weakly, so it needs more laser energy and careful removal of background light.

beyond: Not for the exam. Optical data now validate the spray and combustion models of computational fluid dynamics; kilohertz lasers film single cycles, and tomographic PIV maps the flow in three dimensions. Search next for “optical engine”, “planar laser-induced fluorescence” and “tomographic PIV”.

figure.caption: An optical engine of the Bowditch type. A laser sheet enters through the liner window; light from the chamber goes down through the quartz crown, and the 45° mirror in the extended piston turns it sideways to a camera beside the engine. The two flame outlines are the worked example’s frames, 0.1 ms apart.

spec.aria: Cylinder with liner windows and a laser sheet at 532 nanometres entering from the left. Two flame circles of 8 and 12 millimetres radius. Below, an extended piston with a quartz crown window and a 45 degree mirror reflecting light sideways to a high-speed camera. A side panel computes 40 metres per second and 0.9 degrees of crank angle at 1500 revolutions per minute.
